question: A closed femoral shaft fracture in an adult can cause 1–2 litres of blood loss into the thigh without any external bleeding, sufficient to produce Class III haemorrhagic shock.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is true. The femur is the most vascular long bone; closed femoral shaft fractures reliably cause 1–2 L of concealed haemorrhage. Failure to recognise this leads to underresuscitation. All femoral shaft fractures should be managed as potential haemorrhagic shock.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The thigh can accommodate 1–2 litres of blood in a closed femoral shaft fracture. Class III shock (30–40% blood volume loss, approximately 1.5–2 L in a 70 kg adult) manifests with HR > 120, BP < 90 mmHg, and altered mentation — all from an apparently closed injury.
